FEC shred validation, reconstruction, and completion logic with Merkle and Reed-Solomon checks.

# Purpose
This file implements the `fd_fec_resolver` component, which tracks incoming Solana-style shreds and rebuilds Forward Error Correction sets from them. It defines the resolver state, memory layout, and object life cycle functions such as [`fd_fec_resolver_footprint`](<#fd_fec_resolver_footprint>), [`fd_fec_resolver_new`](<#fd_fec_resolver_new>), [`fd_fec_resolver_join`](<#fd_fec_resolver_join>), [`fd_fec_resolver_leave`](<#fd_fec_resolver_leave>), and [`fd_fec_resolver_delete`](<#fd_fec_resolver_delete>). The resolver keeps a current set map, a done set map, free lists for `fd_fec_set_t` objects and Merkle tree storage, and a SHA-512 context for signature checks. It also stores limits such as `depth`, `partial_depth`, `complete_depth`, `done_depth`, the expected shred version, and the maximum shred index.

The main logic is in [`fd_fec_resolver_add_shred`](<#fd_fec_resolver_add_shred>), which validates each shred, rejects invalid or duplicate input, verifies Merkle proofs and Ed25519 signatures, stores shreds into the correct FEC set, and uses Reed-Solomon recovery to rebuild missing shreds when enough data is present. When a set completes, the code fills missing Merkle proofs and retransmitter signatures, checks that all shreds in the set match the same header fields, and moves the set to the done cache. The file also provides [`fd_fec_resolver_done_contains`](<#fd_fec_resolver_done_contains>), [`fd_fec_resolver_shred_query`](<#fd_fec_resolver_shred_query>), and [`fd_fec_resolver_force_complete`](<#fd_fec_resolver_force_complete>) for lookup and forced completion of a set when only data shreds are present.
